title: The Truth About All-Inclusive Holidays in Baška Voda
metaDescription: Is there all-inclusive in Baška Voda? What it includes, rough € prices per person vs half-board and apartments, and who should skip it. Nearby resorts named.
content:
## Myth 1: Baška Voda is full of all-inclusive resorts

**Reality:** It is not. The town sells mostly half-board, breakfast-only rooms, villas and private apartments. Hotels such as Horizont, Grand Hotel Slavia, Noemia, Aparthotel Milenij and Villa Verica are priced around breakfast or half-board. The one hotel named for all-inclusive is **Hotel Hrvatska (3*)**. It sits at the end of the beach promenade, about 50 m from the beach and roughly 5 minutes' walk from the centre. Central European tour operators sell it with all-inclusive. Availability changes by season and operator, so confirm the board type before paying. Several booking platforms currently show no all-inclusive stock inside the town itself.

**Better alternative:** If all-inclusive is a must, book Hotel Hrvatska only after the operator confirms the board type for your dates. Otherwise go 10–25 km along the coast:

- **Tučepi:** Bluesun Hotel Neptun, all-inclusive, with a pebble beach about 50 m away and a children's pool.
- **Podaca:** Morenia hotel complex, sold as all-inclusive, with children's offers.
- **Drvenik:** Hotel Quercus, all-inclusive, about 100 m from the beach.
- **Živogošće:** TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach, all-inclusive but adults only, so not for families.
- **Omiš (further north):** Sagitta, an all-inclusive-light resort with a kids' club.

## Myth 2: All-inclusive means everything is free

**Reality:** The standard package is breakfast, lunch and dinner as buffets, plus local alcoholic and soft drinks served at a bar. At Hotel Hrvatska the bar runs roughly 10:00–23:00, with tea and coffee at set hours and a light afternoon snack. Imported spirits, à la carte restaurants, excursions, spa and sunbeds usually cost extra. Internet may also be charged.

**Better alternative:** Ask for the drinks list, bar hours and what counts as "local" before booking. A package that stops at 23:00 and excludes coffee between meals is closer to "full board plus drinks".

## Myth 3: All-inclusive is always the cheaper option

**Reality:** These are rough per-person, per-night figures for two adults sharing a room.

| Option | Shoulder (May–June, Sept) | Peak (July–August) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive hotel on the Riviera | about €55–85 | about €100–170 |
| Half-board in a Baška Voda 4* hotel | about €55–70 | about €85–130 |
| Private apartment, self-catering | about €25–40 | about €40–65 |

Short-break all-inclusive packages in Tučepi and Podaca have run about €212–224 per person for 3–4 nights, which is roughly €55–75 per night. Eight-night packages in early June at Drvenik or Podaca are about €573–691 per person, roughly €70–85 a night. Hotel Horizont's half-board plus (drink with dinner included) starts around €56–58 per person in late summer.

**Better alternative:** Half-board lets you eat lunch wherever you are. In an apartment, a family of four often pays less per night than one adult in a peak-season all-inclusive hotel. Apartment prices vary widely by distance from the sea, so treat these figures as a guide.

**Insider perspective:** The cheap all-inclusive prices cluster in May, early June and late September–October. In July and August the gap to half-board widens sharply, and an apartment becomes the clear budget choice.

## Myth 4: All-inclusive suits every family

**Reality:** It suits a narrow group well:

- **Families with children under about 6:** There is no cooking, buffets are flexible, and nobody is hunting for a restaurant at 18:00 with a tired toddler. Children's discounts or free places are common, and Morenia advertises them.
- **Short stays of 3–5 nights:** There is no shopping or planning, and it is easy to budget.
- **Guests who drink moderately:** The drinks value only appears if you use the bar.

It suits worse:

- **Stays of 7+ nights:** Buffet fatigue sets in, and the same hotel food repeats.
- **Guests who want to eat out:** Baška Voda has a long promenade of restaurants, cafés and ice-cream shops, so a package means paying for meals you skip.
- **Families with teenagers or older children:** They want freedom and flexible mealtimes, which a self-catering apartment gives.
- **Light eaters and light drinkers.**

**Better alternative:** Take an apartment close to the promenade and use half-board or all-inclusive only for a few days in a nearby resort if you want a break from cooking.

**Insider perspective:** Baška Voda's strength is its walkable beach strip. Staying put and self-catering uses that strength better than paying for a hotel buffet 15 km away.

## What suits a Baška Voda stay by guest type

For a short break with a small child, pick Hotel Hrvatska if the operator confirms all-inclusive, or Bluesun Neptun in Tučepi if it must be a real resort. For 7 nights or more, a half-board room or an apartment is better. Adults-only guests wanting all-inclusive should look at TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach in Živogošće. Book early for July and August, when all-inclusive rooms near the coast sell out first.

faq.question: But doesn't Baška Voda have all-inclusive resorts like other Croatian coastal towns?
faq.answer: No true resort complexes exist in the town. Hotel Hrvatska (3*) has been sold as all-inclusive by tour operators, while hotels such as Horizont sell half-board. For large all-inclusive resorts, go to Tučepi, Podaca, Drvenik or Živogošće, about 10–25 km away.

faq.question: Isn't all-inclusive always cheaper than paying for meals separately?
faq.answer: No. Shoulder-season all-inclusive runs about €55–85 per person per night, against about €55–70 for half-board and €25–40 per person in an apartment. It only pays off for heavy eaters and drinkers.

faq.question: What is usually included in all-inclusive at Baška Voda area hotels?
faq.answer: Buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner, local alcoholic and soft drinks at a bar (at Hotel Hrvatska about 10:00–23:00), tea and coffee at set hours and a light afternoon snack. Imported drinks, excursions and spa are normally extra.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive good for families with small children?
faq.answer: Yes, especially for stays of 3–7 nights. Meals are flexible, children's pools and discounts are common, and Bluesun Neptun in Tučepi has a children's pool. For longer stays, an apartment is usually better value.

faq.question: Which all-inclusive hotels are closest to Baška Voda?
faq.answer: Bluesun Hotel Neptun in Tučepi, Morenia in Podaca, Hotel Quercus in Drvenik and TUI BLUE Adriatic Beach in Živogošće (adults only). Sagitta in Omiš is further north. All are roughly 10–25 km away.

faq.question: Is the shoulder season really that much cheaper?
faq.answer: Yes. May–June and September–October all-inclusive packages often cost about €55–85 per person per night, while July–August prices can reach €100–170 at beachfront resorts.

quickAnswer: Baška Voda is not an all-inclusive resort town. It is a small Makarska Riviera town of mid-size hotels, villas and apartments. Hotel Hrvatska, a 3-star, has been sold with all-inclusive by Central European tour operators. The big resort-style all-inclusive hotels are 10–25 km away in Tučepi, Podaca, Drvenik and Živogošće.
